observations: The changed line returns a two-element tuple: a SQL string with a single %s placeholder and a one-element parameter tuple (user_id,).
The SQL text is a fixed literal; user_id is not interpolated into the string, so the value is passed as a bound parameter.
The behavior contract states the caller passes the returned SQL and parameter tuple directly to a DB-API driver using %s placeholders, matching the returned shape.
No static findings are reported, so no automated defect signal is present in the supplied data.
For probe p1, query('0 OR 1=1') returns ('SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = %s', ('0 OR 1=1',)); JSON-encoding the tuple as an array yields ["SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = %s", ["0 OR 1=1"]].

A normal comparison input such as query('42') returns ('SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = %s', ('42',)), JSON-encoded as ["SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = %s", ["42"]], differing only in the parameter value.
